To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a series of ternary and mixed ternary graphite intercation compounds containing alkali-metal cations and diamine molecules have been prepared, characterized, and studied by X-ray powder diffraction, infrared, and thermal methods.

we have synthesized and characterized a series of ternary and mixed ternary graphite intercations compounds (GIC) of alkali metals and diamines and have found that the orientation of the diamine molecules is dependent on the cation and that the lattice dimensions of these compounds are dependent on the cations and amines.
a series of ternary and a quaternary GICs of alkali metal and diamine cations have been prepared.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, structure, and properties of a series of ternary and a quaternary GICs of alkali metal and diamine cations.
the synthesis and structure of ternary and mixed ternary GICs containing alkali metal and diamine cations.

the synthesis of ternary and, to a lesser extent, quaternary GICs, with the goal of developing a better understanding of the factors that influence intercalation and the resulting structural and physical properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the intercalation of alkali metals into graphite with diamines results in a series of ternary and mixed ternary compounds, which are characterized by their gallery heights, and that these compounds can be synthesized in high purity and high yield.
the ternary GICs are not simple mixtures of the end-member GICs.
the interlayer gallery height is determined primarily by the alkali metal cation, whereas the orientation of the amine is determined by its size and shape.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ternary GICs are solid solutions with the alkali metal and amine cations randomly distributed, whereas in the quaternary GICs, the two cation types are not mixed.
the intercalation of diamines with alkali metal cation-GICs is highly selective, and the resulting ternary and quaterary compounds are characterized by a range of interlayer dimensions.
, in general, ternary GICs with diamine intercalants are more stable than those with monoamines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intercalated amines are able to accommodate the cations of different sizes and charge states, and the resulting compounds are solid solutions.
the alkali metal cation and amine can be intercalated independently, and the resulting compounds are not solid solutions.
the alkali cation is not the only factor that determines the orientation of intercalated molecules, and that the presence of a diamine in the GIC can induce a chelation of the intercalated cations.
